rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In recurring resurrection scenes, passive verbs and figurative attribution foreground the event; the cosmos is already subjected, so events unfold spontaneously without an explicit agent.
rows.anchor: البناء للمجهول تركيز للإهتمام بالحدث، بصرف النظر عن محدثه. وفي الإسناد المجازي أو المطاوعة، تقرير لوقوع الأحاث في طواعية تلقائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zalzala denotes violent movement and severe agitation, first used physically and later for calamities and terrors.
rows.anchor: الزلزلة في اللغة، الحركة العنيفة والإضطراب الشديد: استعمل في الحسيات، فقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root occurs six times: three times for the Last Day's terror and three times for intense wartime distress and panic.
rows.anchor: وردت المادة، فعلاً ومصدراً ست مرات: ثلاثاً منها في وصف يوم الهول الأكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreters say the agent is omitted because known, but this misses the recurring style: elsewhere the Qur'an freely names God as agent even when known.
rows.anchor: قال مفسرون: إن الفاعل حذف للعلم به، غير ملتفتين إلى أنها ظاهرة أسلوبية مطردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense asserts the event's certainty; idha projects it into the future while retaining the past's force, and its suddenness suits the unexpected Last Day.
rows.anchor: ومجيء الفعل ماضياً، تقرير لأنه حادث فعلاً. وقد صدر بإذا، فصرفته إلى المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects attempts to supply an implicit governing verb after idha because they distract from the sudden shock, certainty, and focus on the event.
rows.anchor: سر البيان وراء كل هذا، ولأن مناط القوة في التعبير هو بغتة المفأجاة، وتأكيد الحدث

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority, including the seven canonical imams, read zalzalah with kasra; another reading has fatha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور {زِلْزَالَهَا} بكسر الزاى وهي قراءة الأئمة السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasra makes the word a verbal noun, while fatha makes it a noun; she prefers the verbal noun because its emphasis fits the context and parallels Ahzab 33:11.
rows.anchor: والمصدرية أولى بالمقام، لما فيها من تأكيد يلائم السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the earthquake to the earth fits the spontaneous action in the following extraction and speech, and points to the familiar, full measure of its quake.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الزلزال إلى ضمير الأرض، متسق مع التلقائية الملحوظة في هذه الآية وما بعدها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses it as the earth's severe earthquake, with no earthquake after it; the author accepts this gloss.
rows.anchor: ولا بأس بما قاله الزمخشري هنا من أنه "زلزالها الشديد الذي ليس بعده زلزال"

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the earth is assigned the quake it deserves by its mass and nature, excluding any lesser quake; the author accepts the point.
rows.anchor: وأضيف الزلزال إلى الأرض، إذا المعنى زلزالها الي تستحقه ويقتضيه جرمها وعظمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the inanimate earth the grammatical agent continues the depiction of its willing submission and keeps attention on the event rather than its source.
rows.anchor: جعل الأرض هنا فاعلة. وهي جماد، مضياً في تقرير مطاوعتها، وكونها مسخرة لمثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the word earth is deliberate, reinforcing certainty and psychological persuasion.
rows.anchor: وتكرار الأرض هنا مقصود، لترسيخ اليقين، والإقناع النفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athqal means heavy burdens, the opposite of lightness; lexicographers and exegetes agree, and al-Raghib traces its use from physical bodies to figurative burdens.
rows.anchor: والأثقال جمع ثقل، وهو الحمل الشديد. واللغويون والمفسرون، متفقون على أن الثقل هنا نقيض الحفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses burdens physically for what livestock carry and figuratively for sins, as well as for the earth's burdens here.
rows.anchor: وجاءت "الأثقال" في القرآن في ثلاث آيات: آية النحل 7

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the earth's burdens as buried treasures, figuratively called its heavy contents.
rows.anchor: ونص في (الأساس) على أن هذا من المجاز، جعل ما في جوفها من الجفائن أثقالاً لها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view reported in al-Bahr includes both treasures and the dead; the author rejects the treasure timing and the contrived theory of two earthquakes.
rows.anchor: وفي (البحر المحيط) مما قيل في الآية، أن أثقالها كنوزها وموتاها

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi explains the earth's burdens as the dead alone.
rows.anchor: وأكتفى "الطبرسي" في تفسير الأثقال بالموتى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib reports two explanations: the earth's treasures, or the human bodies it contains for resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال "الراغب": قيل كنوزها، وقيل ما تصمنته من أجساد البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than specify the contents, she reads the image as the earth eagerly shedding a crushing load when the time arrives, reinforced by the earth casting out and emptying itself in 84:3.
rows.anchor: ما توحى به من إندفاع للتخلص من الثقل الباهظ، فالمثقل يتلهف على التخفف من حمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reducing the phrase to whatever is inside the earth erases the vivid image of a burdened bearer longing to rid itself of its load.
rows.anchor: والتأويل بـ: وأخرجت الأرض ما في جوفها، يضيع به هذا الإيحاء المثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing extraction to the earth alongside the passive quake continues the image of an automatic event that needs no stated agent and foregrounds the action.
rows.anchor: إسناد الإخراج مجازاً إلى الأرض، مع {زُلْزِلَتِ} على البناء للمجهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question conveys wonder, astonishment, fear, anxiety, and tense expectation.
rows.anchor: السؤال واضح فيه معنى العجب والدهشة، والخوف والقلق والترقب

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn takes the question as denial, which the author rejects because the resurrection is already happening after its warnings.
rows.anchor: من المفسرين - كما في الجلالين - من ذهب إلى أن الاستفهام إنكاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insan is humanity in general, struck by the violent quake and release of the earth's burdens, and asking in amazement what is happening.
rows.anchor: والإنسان هنا هو الإنسان، على الإطلاق، تروعه الزلزلة العنيفة وما أعقبها من لإخراج الأرض أثقالها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Many exegetes, whom Abu Hayyan calls the majority, limit the human to the disbeliever who denied resurrection; the author rejects this as unsupported and weaker than a universal shock.
rows.anchor: وصرح "أبو حيان" في (البحر) بأن هذا هو مذهب الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal reading is supported by the Hajj description, where nursing mothers, pregnant women, and people generally are terrified by the quake.
rows.anchor: ويؤنس إلى هذا الإطلاق والتعميم، قوله تعالى في وصف الزلزلة، في آية الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terror reaches all people, as the Hajj passage says every nursing mother is distracted, every pregnant woman delivers, and people appear drunk.
rows.anchor: تذهل كل مرضعة، وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها، وترى الناس، عاكة الناس، لا الكفار وحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawma'idhin strongly recalls the preceding description so the audience connects the coming statement with the scene already described.
rows.anchor: وسر التعبير بيومئذ هنا، أنه لفت قوي يستحضر معه السامع ما مضى من وصف اليوم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reads the earth's reporting as figurative: its unprecedented transformation itself informs and answers the questioner.
rows.anchor: الإمام الطبري يذهب إلى أن تحدث الأرض هنا تمثيل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likewise treats reporting metaphorically, as God's creation of conditions that function like verbal speech; Muhammad Abduh is said to agree.
rows.anchor: والتحدث مجاز عن إحداث الله تعالى فيها من الأحوال ما يقوم مقام التحديث باللسان

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says that when people ask what is wrong, the earth tells them worldly life has ended and the afterlife has come, answering their question.
rows.anchor: فتخبر أن أمر الدنيا قد أنقضى، وأن أمر الآخرة قد أتى، فيكون ذلك جواباً لهم عن سؤالهم

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi offers three possibilities: God creates speech in the earth, turns it into a speaking animal, or manifests something that serves as speech.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون الله تعالى أحدث الكلام فيها، ويجوز أن يقلبها حيواناً يقدر على النطق

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والثوري
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and al-Thawri are named as holders of the literal view that the earth is given life and perception to speak.
rows.anchor: وهو قول إبن مسعود والثوري وغيرهما

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet explained that the earth's news is its testimony for each person about deeds performed on its surface on particular days; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: إن أخبارها أن تشهد على كل عبد أو أمة بما عمل على ظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic eloquence gives inanimate things active, speaking, willing, perceptive personalities, as it does with Hell.
rows.anchor: بل يجرد منه كذلك شخصية حية، فاعلة ناطقة، مريدة مدركة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Because tuhaddith can take two objects, Abu Hayyan says its omitted first object is people: the earth tells people its news; the next verse makes the meaning clear.
rows.anchor: وعند أبي حيان أن المحذوف أو لهما، أي تحدث الناس أخبارها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls God's revelation to the earth metaphorical, like the creative command Be.
rows.anchor: والإيحاء عند "الزمخشري" مجاز، كقوله تعالى: {أَنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ}

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi explains the revelation as God inspiring and informing the earth that it should report its news.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبرسي في مجمع البيان: "أوحى لها، أي ألهمها وعرفها بأن تحدث أخبارها"

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: Muhammad Abduh takes the revelation as a special divine creative command telling the earth to become ruined, like the command that first made it earth.
rows.anchor: الوحي هم الأمر الإلهي الخاص، قال لها: كوني خراباً، كما قال لها عند إيجادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These explanations are close and acceptable, but command or speech alone misses the word's quick and hidden force; al-Raghib best captures its Arabic and Qur'anic sense.
rows.anchor: وهي أقوال متقاربة ومقبولة وإن لم يكف تفسير الوحي بالأمر، أو القول، لتبين أثر اللفظ

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines wahy as a rapid, hidden sign: inspiration for a living recipient and subjection for an inanimate one.
rows.anchor: الوحي الإشارة السريعة مع الخفاء، فإن كان الموحي إليه حياً فهو إلهام، وإن كان جماداً فهو تسخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic uses wahy for haste and decisive speed, including the saying that death by sword is faster and more decisive.
rows.anchor: ومن أمثالهم: الموت بالسيف أوحى، أي أسرع وأحسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also connotes secrecy; hiddenness and speed give rise to its sense of inspiration, whose source is obscure and onset rapid.
rows.anchor: ومن الخفاء والسرعة الملحوظين في المادة، جاء الوحي بمعنى الإلهام بملحظ من خفاء مصدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses wahy for hidden inspiration to a person in God's communication to humans and to Moses' mother.
rows.anchor: والقرآن استعمل الوحي في خفي الإلهام في: آية الشورى 51

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unexpressed recipient has been proposed: God revealed to the angels assigned to earth to make these events happen; another explanation makes the lam causal.
rows.anchor: وقيل الموحى إليه محذوف، أي أوحى إلى ملائكته المصرفين أن تفعل بالأرض تلك الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation to the bee in 16:68 exemplifies wahy as subjection, while the Qur'an most often uses wahy for revelation to prophets.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى التسخير في آية النحل 68

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here wahy is not a spoken command: command implies directed speech and lacks the word's speed and secrecy; God instead deposits a capacity in the earth.
rows.anchor: ليس الوحي بمعنى الأمر، لأن الأمر يقتضي توجيه الحديث ويعوزه ما للوحي من دلالة السرعة والخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across 71 Qur'anic uses, the verb omits its recipient twice, takes ila 67 times, fi once, and lam only here.
rows.anchor: فنراه استعمل الفهل إحدى وسبعين مرة:

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the lam may answer the verse's rhyme; since revelation to earth is at issue, he allows inspiration or an angelic messenger.
rows.anchor: وعدى أوحى باللام، وإن كان المشهور تعديتها بإلى، لمراعاة الفواصل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan continues that revelation to the earth could be inspiration or could arrive through an angelic messenger.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان الإيحاء إليها أحتمل أن يكون وحي إلهام، وأحتمل أن يكون برسول من الملائكة

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham cites the verse to show that lam can correspond to ila, as it can correspond to several other prepositions in eloquent Arabic.
rows.anchor: جاء بالآية شاهداً على أن اللام تأتي موافقة لإلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her Qur'anic survey distinguishes recipients: living beings take ila, while inanimate recipients take fi, as with the skies, or lam, as with the earth here.
rows.anchor: أما الجماد فلا يتعدى الوحي إليه بحرف إلى، بل بحرف في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 41:12, fi indicates God placed each sky's ordering within it, establishing its system; the locative preposition signals this enabling and arrangement.
rows.anchor: أي بث فيها، ما به نظامها، فعدى الفعل بـ (في) الظرفية التي تدل على التمكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects the grammarians' claim that one preposition simply substitutes for another, since that would erase distinctions essential to expressive language.
rows.anchor: ويراه خاصة من فقهاء العربية مبطلاً لحقيقة اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects the rhyme explanation: the Qur'an does not choose a word for sound alone without a meaning that requires it.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم، بل لا نعرف أن هذا البيان المعجز، يؤثر كلمة على غيرها لمجرد ملحظ لفظي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hidden angelic recipient would insert an intermediary where the context stresses the earth's direct, spontaneous agency and ability to speak.
rows.anchor: لا وجه لتقدير وساطة الملائكة، لإيصال الإيحاء إلى الأرض التي زلزلت زلزالها، وأخرجت أثقالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's direct revelation answers the human question through the earth itself; lam adds specificity, attachment, becoming, and force to the connection.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا كان إيثار التعدية باللام، لما في معنى اللام من اختصاص، وإلصاق، وصيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawma'idhin returns the reader to the earlier scene, linking the resurrection's successive moments and reviving prior warnings.
rows.anchor: يومئذ: كرة راجعة إلى ما قبل، يصل بها القرآن مشاهد الموقف، ويرد السامع إلى ما سبق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Most exegetes, including al-Zamakhshari, take people yasdur to mean they emerge from their graves; al-Jalalayn and al-Tabrisi say they leave the place of reckoning.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المفسريمن على أن {يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ} هنا بمعنى يخرجون من القبور "الزمخشري"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She insists that sudur means the opposite of wurud, arrival at water: worldly life is a temporary journey, and one must prepare to depart from it.
rows.anchor: لا أجد ما يفسر به الصدر في آية الزلزلة، إلا نقيض الورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic pairing of arriving at Midian's water with shepherds later departing from it supports the contrast between wurud and sudur; Abu Hayyan also notes this relation.
rows.anchor: وأبو جيان، قد صرح بأن "الصدر يكون عن ورد"

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says that when sudur is used with an, it means departure; Muhammad Abduh likewise glosses it as leaving a city, but the author finds this insufficient.
rows.anchor: وإذا عدى صدر بعن، اقتضى الانصراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She accepts only the sense opposite to arrival: the Qur'an uses sudur in just the Midian and Resurrection passages.
rows.anchor: ولا نطمئن إلى شيء في تفسير الصدر إلا أنه مقابل الورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People scattered apart are more confused, frightened, and fearful because separation removes the comfort and hope, even illusory, of company.
rows.anchor: وكونهم يصدرون "أشتاتاً" أي متفرقين، أدعى للحيرة والخوف والرهبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashtat is the plural of shatt, dispersal or difference; the Qur'an uses the root five times, with shatta three times and ashtatan twice.
rows.anchor: وأشتات: جمع شت، والشت والشتات في اللغة التفرق والاختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashtat means dispersion opposite to gathering, while shatta emphasizes variety and difference.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التفرق، المقابل للتجمع، واضح في الآيتين، أما شتى غالملحوظ فيها التنوع والاختلاف

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib glosses ashtatan as scattered apart; this fits the parallel Qur'anic depictions of people scattered like locusts or moths.
rows.anchor: وبالتفرق، فسر "الراغب" أشتاتاً في آية الزلزلة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers remote alternatives: people may have white or black faces in fear, or separate onto the paths to Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: أشتاتاً: بيض الوجوه أو سود الوجوه فزعين

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan glosses ashtatan simply as groups or divisions.
rows.anchor: أشتاتاً، جمع شت، أي فرقاً

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi says people return from the reckoning in groups divided by faith and by religion.
rows.anchor: أهل الإيمان على حدة، وأهل كل دين على حدة

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: Muhammad Abduh interprets the groups as people of different fates: fortunate or wretched, righteous or sinful.
rows.anchor: على اختلافهم، شقيهم وسعيدهم، محسنهم ومسيئهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those alternatives add little; the basic sense of dispersion itself heightens terror and rebuke by depriving people of companionship.
rows.anchor: وإنما تقوي الإثارة والتلاهيب والردع، حين يكون من التشتت بمعنى التفرق والبعثرة والإنتشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispersed people are being led to see their deeds.
rows.anchor: وهم يصدرون أشتاتاً {لِيُرَوْا أَعْمَالَهُمْ}

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: A reading has the verb active, but the majority reading is passive; the author says the passive matches the scene's focus and people being led to the gathering.
rows.anchor: ولكن الجمهور على قراءة الأئمة بالبناء للمجهول، وهي الظاهرة على السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mithqal is what is used for weighing and appears eight times; with mustard seed in two verses, context suggests minute size and concealment rather than light weight.
rows.anchor: والسياق في الآيتين يرجح، والله أعلم، أن المقصود بمثقال حبة من خردل هنا، ليس بخفة الوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the two mustard-seed passages and the hiddenness contexts, she reads minute size; in the four remaining passages, including these verses, dharra means extreme lightness of weight.
rows.anchor: على حين تتعين دلالة {مِثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ} على خفة الوزن في الآيات الأربع التالية

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Tha'lab says one hundred dharra weigh as much as a grain of barley.
rows.anchor: إن مائة منها، وزن حبة شعير

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan identifies dharra as a small, thin, red ant.
rows.anchor: إنها النملة الصغيرة، حمراء رقيقة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports that dharra may mean a tiny ant or dust visible in a sunbeam; Muhammad Abduh gives a similar explanation.
rows.anchor: "قيل هي النملة الصغيرة، وقيا: الذر ما يرى في شعاع الشمس من الهباء"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects exact measurements as the Qur'an's intent and especially rejects the modern claim that the word means the scientifically discovered atom.
rows.anchor: وقد حاول محاولون أن يعينوا مقدار الذرة على وجه التحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She prefers the Arabic sense of utmost smallness and lightness, evoked by scattered grains, motes in sunlight, and tiny ants, rather than exact physical dimensions.
rows.anchor: ونؤثر أن نفهمها بحس العربية على هدى البيان القرآني، دون تكلف لتقدير الأوزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first Arabic audience understood mithqal dharra as an extreme of tiny size and lightness, even a mote without weight.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه التناهي في الضآلة والخفة والصغر، حتى ليكون من الهباء الذي لا وزن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This minute measure suits the surah's imagery of quake, eruption, fragmentation, and dispersal: burdens emerge, people scatter, and even tiny deeds are seen.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يلائم، مادياً وبياناً، جو الموقف ونسق السياق، من الزلزلة والإنفجار والتفتيت والتشتيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theology raised a problem: if disbelief cancels good deeds and avoiding major sins forgives minor ones, why are tiny good and evil deeds mentioned?
rows.anchor: حسنات الكافر محبطة بالكفر، وسيئات المؤمن معفوة بإجتناب الكبائر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilite al-Zamakhshari restricts the good deed to a member of the saved group.
rows.anchor: فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيراً من فريق السعداء

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan restricts the good deed to believers among the saved and generalizes the evil deed; he cites Ibn Abbas that believers see their deeds, while disbelievers' worldly good is already paid and believers' lesser sins are expiated by worldly hardships.
rows.anchor: وقال إبن عباس: هذه الأعمال في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi argues that the apparent meaning refutes annulment of deeds: every act of obedience or sin receives recompense.
rows.anchor: طاهرها يدل على أنه لا يفعل أحد شيئاً من طاعة أو معصية، إلا ويجازى علية

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: Muhammad Abduh says the verses reassure believers that no small good deed escapes notice and even a tiny sin matters.
rows.anchor: فالخير يجازى به مهما صغر، والشر يلقى جزاءه مهما نزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These readings do not settle the issue in light of verses affirming that God may forgive any sin short of associating partners and forgives all sins.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some resolve the problem by saying a believer sees punishment in worldly life, or by limiting punishment to evil left without repentance.
rows.anchor: مما أضطر بعضهم إلى القول بأن "المؤمن يرى عقوبته في الدنيا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She says the theological dispute is not really what these verses address and illustrates the need for a methodical study of Qur'anic word meanings.
rows.anchor: ما الذي أقحم قضية الإحباط ومسألة الحساب على آيتي الزلزلة، وليستا متعلقتين بجزاء أو عقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She asks why annulment and accounting were brought into these verses when they do not concern recompense or punishment.
rows.anchor: ما الذي أقحم قضية الإحباط ومسألة الحساب على آيتي الزلزلة، وليستا متعلقتين بجزاء أو عقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses say deeds are seen, not recompensed or judged; the preceding verse confirms that every deed is precisely presented, with nothing small or great omitted.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل تعالى: {يجز به أو يحاسب عليه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment and recompense come afterward according to God's justice, favor, and mercy.
rows.anchor: ثم يكون الحساب والجزاء بعد ذلك بعدل الله وفضله ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The short verses race through the raid's stages from the charge to its decisive attack on the gathering, conveying its violence and sudden surprise.
rows.anchor: ليس بين العدو الذي هو مرحلة الإبتداء، وإقتحام الجمع الذي هو ذروة الإغارة، إلا ما بين هذه الآيات القصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qur'anic battle imagery, jam'an often means a large force and suggests strength and victory.
rows.anchor: هذا اللفظ يأتي كثيراً في القرآن، للحشد الكاثر في المعركة، ومع مظنة القوة والغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls the Last Day the Day of Gathering because all creation is assembled after resurrection, and also calls the place of reckoning a gathering.
rows.anchor: وسمى اليوم الآخر في القرآن يوم الجمع، لاحتشاد الخلق به بعد بعثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanud is unique in Qur'anic form and root; lexically it means ungrateful for blessings, stingy, or disobedient, perhaps originally describing barren land.
rows.anchor: الكنود وحيدة في القرآن. صيغة ومادة. وهو في اللغة: الكفور للنعمة، والبخيل، والعاصي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports dialectal meanings: disobedient among Kinda, stingy among Banu Malik, and ungrateful among Mudar and Rabi'a.
rows.anchor: الكنود بلسان كندة: العاصي، وبلسان بني مالك: البخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meanings cohere with the image of infertile land, and ungratefulness for God's blessings is closest to this verse, as al-Raghib also says.
rows.anchor: وأقرب معانيها إلى آية العاديات، والله أعلم أنه الكفران بنعمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human bears witness against himself to ingratitude, a damning admission used for warning and threat, as in verses where people acknowledge their own disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي يشهد على نفسه بكفران نعمة ربه، وليس أقوى منها شهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic scenes of body parts testifying support the reading that the human himself witnesses to his ingratitude.
rows.anchor: يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahada originally means presence or witnessing; a person's confession compels acknowledgment and prevents denial or claims of innocence.
rows.anchor: وأصل الشهادة في اللغة من الشهود أي الحضور، والمشاهدة: المعاينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes make God the subject of the witness clause, but the author rejects this because the human's testimony against himself is stronger and matches the parallel verses.
rows.anchor: إن الضمير في {وَإِنَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ} يعود إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those exegetes then switch the pronoun to the human in the next verse, breaking the unity of the three verses; they also gloss khayr as money, citing the bequest verse.
rows.anchor: فتمزقت بهذا الصنيع وحدة السياق في الآيات الثلاث

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib restricts khayr meaning wealth to a large amount of money.
rows.anchor: لا يقال للمال خير حتى يكون كثيراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Qur'anic contexts may support wealth as khayr, and the word once refers to horses in David's speech.
rows.anchor: وجاء الخير مرة واحدة للخيل في آية (ص 32) على لسان داود:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Qur'anic uses of khayr mean better or best, about 125 occurrences, often with a comparative construction.
rows.anchor: على أن لفظ الخير، أكثر ما يستعمل في القرآن بمعنى الأفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr also explicitly contrasts with evil in several passages.
rows.anchor: كما يأتي في القرآن، نقضاً للشر صراحة في مثل آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr can also contrast with harm and misfortune, as in the cited passages.
rows.anchor: أو مقابلاً بالسوء والضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic permits khayr to mean wealth, horses, the opposite of evil, or goodness and virtue.
rows.anchor: واللغة تحتمل أن يكون الخير للمال، والخيل، وضد الشر، والخيار والفضيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context favors material wealth: an ungrateful person who testifies to his own ingratitude would intensely love money, not virtue.
rows.anchor: غير أنسياق آية (العاديات) يرجح أن الخير فيها هو الخير المادي من مال أو شبهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shadd originally means a strong knot or binding, physically and metaphorically, as the cited verses show.
rows.anchor: والأصل في الشد: قوة العقد والوثاق والإحكام، مادياً كما في آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses the phrase reaching one's full maturity and strength for growing into adulthood in several passages.
rows.anchor: كما يعبر القرآن، عمن بلوغ الرشد والقوة بصيغة: بلغ أو يبلغ أشده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shadid appears about forty times with punishment, divine might, seizure, or afterlife retribution, usually as warning and rebuke.
rows.anchor: فجاءت في القرآن، في نحو أربعين موضعاً، مضافة إلى عذاب الله، وبطشه، وأخذه، وعقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exceptional uses describe iron, Lot's wished-for strong support, Solomon's threatened punishment, and strong fighting forces.
rows.anchor: وجاءت مرة وصفاً للحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative ashad usually describes severity or force; its sole use for love is believers' greater love for God in 2:165.
rows.anchor: وجاءت مرة واحدة مميزة بالحب في آية البقرة 165

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's usual threatening use of shidda adds menace to the interpreters' gloss of withholding and stinginess, in light of the preceding self-witness.
rows.anchor: يضيف بلا شك، إلى ما اكتفى المفسرون به في آية العاديات، من معنى البخل والإمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afala ya'lam gives the passage a forceful warning and rebuke.
rows.anchor: بما فيها من نذير صادع وزجر رادع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ba'thara occurs only here and in 82:4; both describe graves scattered at resurrection in the passive, foregrounding the event and swiftly moving to reckoning.
rows.anchor: وكلتاهما في بعثرة القبور يوم القيامة، وفيهما جاء الفعل مبنياً للمجهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ba'thara can mean scattering, mixing, turning something upside down, exposing its contents, or even the turmoil of nausea.
rows.anchor: والبعثرة لغة، فيها معنى التبديد والتفريق والإختلاط، وقلب بعض الشيء على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary sense is dispersal and confusion, with a latent sense of uncovering and investigation that prepares for exposing what is in people's breasts.
rows.anchor: والمتبادر من مفهوم {بعثر} في آيتي العايات والإنفطار، هو التشتت والتفرق والإنتثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hussila is also passive, keeping attention on the event itself, and the root h-s-l occurs only in this surah.
rows.anchor: وقد جيء به فور البعثرة، مبنياً للمجهول كذلك، صرفاً عن كل ما عدا الحدث نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hussila evokes gathering and retaining in the depths: a person's deeds remain stored within until revealed after the graves are scattered.
rows.anchor: فكل ما يعمله الإنسان مستقر في أعماقه، مجموع في صدره، حتى يحين أوان كشفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase what is in the breasts signals disclosure of hidden contents, as Qur'anic usage depicts thoughts and secrets concealed within.
rows.anchor: إيذاناً بكشف المستور وإظهار المطوى المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects the interpretation that deeds are merely gathered in records: the scene warns that hidden inner contents will be exposed.
rows.anchor: ليس المقام هنا للجمع في الصحف، وإنما المقام للإنذار بيوم ينكشف فيه ما طوى في الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final declaration of God's awareness follows the scattering of graves and disclosure of hearts, bringing the violent scene to its peak.
rows.anchor: بعد بعثرة ما في القبور وتحصيل ما في الصدور، فتصل بالمشهد المثير إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no need to read khabir as meaning that God will recompense people; the Qur'an uses khabir only as God's name or attribute, about forty-five times.
rows.anchor: ولسنا هنا بحاجة إلى القول بتضمن خبير لمعنى "مجاز لهم في ذلك اليوم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabir is not a precise synonym for alim, since the two are paired, as are khabir with hakim and basir.
rows.anchor: وتفسيره بالعليم غير دقيق، إذ جاء الخبير مقترناً بالعليم في آية التحريم 3

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabir is uniquely divine, unlike alim, which describes created people too; that exclusivity points to a more particular kind of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وتفرد الله وحده بوصف {الْخَبِيرُ} - وليس الأمر كذلك في العليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabr has sensory associations with a water spring at a mountain's base and good first-cut wool; to test something is to examine it and learn its true nature.
rows.anchor: وأختبرت الشيء أو الشخص. فحصته وأمتحنته لتعرف حقيقة أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using khabir after the disclosure of hearts, with emphatic inna and lam, brings the threat to its height and leaves the imagination to picture the warning.
rows.anchor: وإيثار لفظ {خَبِير} هنا، بعد أن {حُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ} ، مع تأكيده باللام وإن في أول الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She finds a striking, previously unnoticed connection between the opening violent raid and the closing scene of graves and hearts laid bare.
rows.anchor: وهذه الوقفة الحاسمة، يبلغ بها القرآن ذروة المشهد العنيف لبعثرة ما في القبور وتحصيل ما في الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah opens by evoking the familiar sudden raid at dawn, before its targets notice the raiders have entered and scattered their gathering in dust.
rows.anchor: تبدأ بواو لبقسم لافته في قوة إلى المشهد المألوف، لإغارة عنيفة مفاجئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A familiar raid's panic provides an image for the unseen resurrection: people are scattered from graves, depart in groups, and face rapid, linked events culminating before the All-Aware.
rows.anchor: ذلك هو مشهد البعث، يباغت القوم - وقد طال ما جحدوا نعمة الله وغرتهم الأماني -
